library_preparation_preflight.summary: The failure is a namespace mismatch, not missing setup. The 9.0.x tests import javax.servlet and javax.websocket, but tomcat-embed-websocket 10.0.0 is the Jakarta EE 9 line and uses jakarta.servlet and jakarta.websocket. Nothing beyond the normal generated test scaffold is needed.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Write the 10.0.0 tests against the jakarta.* namespace. Replace javax.websocket.*, javax.websocket.server.* and javax.servlet.* (including javax.servlet.descriptor.*) with their jakarta.* equivalents, and do not copy the 9.0.x test sources verbatim. The existing build.gradle needs no change. It already declares the tomcat-embed-websocket dependency at the tested version, and tomcat-embed-websocket 10.0.0 should pull in tomcat-embed-core transitively, which supplies jakarta.servlet. I did not resolve the 10.0.0 POM or jar to confirm this, so if jakarta.servlet is missing at compile time, add org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core at the same version as testImplementation. Keep the agent configuration with conditional mode and user-code-filter.json, and check that the filter's package names still match the test packages. Tomcat 10 also dropped some 9.x behavior, so re-check any 9.x-specific class or method usage (WsSci, WsServerContainer and the like) against the 10.0.0 sources.
risks: The reproducer names 9.0.83 while the issue targets 10.0.0, so the harness may have copied the javax-based tests into the 10.0.0 project. The tests must be rewritten rather than reused.
I did not resolve the 10.0.0 POM or jar. Whether tomcat-embed-core arrives transitively is an assumption from Tomcat's usual packaging.
The Jakarta API surface in 10.0.0 may differ slightly from 9.x, for example in ServletContext methods that the WsSciTest stub implements, so the stubs may need adjusting.
